cluster_summary: This cluster covers vulnerabilities arising from improper handling of user-supplied data during cookie parsing and output generation. Common issues include missing validation of control characters in Set-Cookie headers, unsafe deserialization of cookie data using pickle, prototype pollution from untrusted cookie names, over-broad whitespace trimming causing normalization bypass, and missing output encoding leading to XSS. These flaws allow attackers to inject arbitrary headers, execute arbitrary code, pollute object prototypes, bypass security prefixes, or perform cross-site scripting.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-controlled markup, HTML fragments, rich text, comments, DOM nodes, style blocks, attributes, or URI values into HTML cleaners, SafeHtml validators, DOM sanitizers, rich-text renderers, or browser-rendered sanitized output. Report code paths where the active sanitizer policy does not allowlist dangerous elements, attributes, URI schemes, DOM child nodes, comments, or malformed inputs before rendering. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should activate the restrictive sanitizer for the relevant mode, enforce element/attribute/URI allowlists after parsing, and add regression tests for the bypass form.

mechanism.missing_guard: the active sanitizer policy does not allowlist dangerous elements, attributes, URI schemes, DOM child nodes, comments, or malformed inputs before rendering
mechanism.name: HTML sanitizer policy gap or inactive allowlist
mechanism.sink_shape: HTML cleaners, SafeHtml validators, DOM sanitizers, rich-text renderers, or browser-rendered sanitized output
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-controlled markup, HTML fragments, rich text, comments, DOM nodes, style blocks, attributes, or URI values
mechanism.typical_fix: activate the restrictive sanitizer for the relevant mode, enforce element/attribute/URI allowlists after parsing, and add regression tests for the bypass form

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Apply a whitelist regex and length limit to restrict allowed characters in the parameter before constructing the cookie.
sub_patterns.name: Missing input validation for cookie parameter leading to reflected XSS
sub_patterns.root_cause: User-supplied query parameter is directly used as cookie key/value in Set-Cookie header without validation or encoding, allowing injection of HTML/JavaScript that is later reflected.
